_comment: Canonical bibliographic registry for the biological data (V2.42). Every `source` string in plant_fauna_master.json, bee_attributes_master.json and lepidoptera_attributes_master.json resolves to a key here, so the app can render a real citation instead of a shorthand and a reader can go and check the claim. Keys are stable identifiers, never displayed.
_honesty: `record_confidence` describes THIS BIBLIOGRAPHIC ENTRY, not the ecological claims that cite it. 'verified' = the author/title/year/publisher below have been checked against the work or a library catalogue. 'unverified' = transcribed from the shorthand citation already in the seed data and NOT yet checked; the work is real and the citation is genuine, but a detail here (an edition year, a publisher) may be wrong. Per P9 we ship the distinction rather than a uniform-looking table that hides it. Do not promote an entry to 'verified' without actually checking it.
_p9: Nothing in this file certifies an ecological claim. It makes each claim traceable to a work a reader can obtain. Whether that work supports the specific edge citing it is a separate question, unanswerable from inside this repository - see docs/DATA_AUDIT.md section 7.

sources.title: Unattributed prairie-composite pollination literature
sources.record_note: THIS IS NOT A CITATION AND MUST NOT BE RENDERED AS ONE. The 16 edges carrying this key were seeded with the source string 'Prairie-composite pollination literature; Acorn & Sheldon 2006', whose first half names no work. The Acorn & Sheldon half is real and is why these edges are not simply wrong, but the original author cited two things and only one of them can be checked - so promoting these edges to the Acorn & Sheldon key would assert a coverage that was never claimed. They are parked here instead, visible and countable, until somebody re-sources them. Doing so is the single highest-value citation task in the repository.

sources.authors: Poelen, J.H., Simons, J.D. and Miller, C.J.
sources.title: Global Biotic Interactions: An open infrastructure to share and analyze species-interaction datasets
sources.record_note: An AGGREGATOR, not a primary work, and the edges filed under it are weaker evidence than the field guides above. GloBI collates interaction records from hundreds of datasets; the 2,546 edges added in V2.59 were fetched from its /interaction endpoint, which returns distinct interactions WITHOUT the reporting study. Each is independently checkable by querying GloBI for the same pair, which is why it qualifies as documented — but the specific paper behind each record is not yet captured. Re-fetching with includeObservations=true would upgrade these in place; tracked as F125b.
